chunks: And from him, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Nusayr ibn Kathir, from Abu Basir, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was saying: 'A dirham spent in Hajj is superior to two thousand [dirhams] in other paths of Allah.'

key_terms.دِرْهَمٌ: A silver coin, representing a small amount of money
key_terms.سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: In the path of Allah, referring to acts of worship and charity

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual merit of spending money for Hajj compared to other acts of worship?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the unique spiritual weight of Hajj by comparing a single dirham spent on it to two thousand dirhams in other acts of worship. This comparison underscores the principle that the merit of an act is often determined by the specific command of the Lawgiver rather than merely the quantity of wealth expended, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding the superiority of obligatory acts over voluntary ones.
